chapters.title: Solomon is proclaimed king before Adonijah can seize power

parts.text: The aged David is cared for by Abishag. Adonijah exalts himself as the next king, gaining Joab and Abiathar’s support and holding a feast that excludes Solomon and David’s loyal servants. Nathan alerts Bath-sheba and arranges for both to inform David, recalling his oath that Solomon would succeed him. They warn that Adonijah’s claim places Solomon and Bath-sheba in danger.

David orders Zadok, Nathan, and Benaiah to take Solomon on the royal mule to Gihon, anoint him, and proclaim him king. The public celebration interrupts Adonijah’s feast with news that David has confirmed Solomon’s rule. Adonijah’s guests scatter, and he seeks sanctuary at the altar. Solomon grants conditional mercy, telling him to go home and prove himself worthy.

chapters.title: David’s final charge and Solomon’s kingdom established

parts.text: David charges Solomon to be strong and obey the LORD’s law, linking the dynasty’s continuance to faithful conduct. He also gives instructions concerning Joab’s bloodshed, kindness toward Barzillai’s sons, and Shimei’s earlier curses. David dies after forty years of rule, and Solomon sits on an increasingly established throne.

Adonijah asks through Bath-sheba to marry Abishag, which Solomon treats as another claim to the kingdom and punishes with death. Abiathar is removed from the priesthood, fulfilling the word against Eli’s house. Joab is executed despite taking hold of the altar, answering for innocent blood. Shimei is confined to Jerusalem under oath; when he leaves and returns, Solomon orders his death. Benaiah and Zadok receive the vacated offices.

chapters.title: Solomon asks for wisdom and judges between two mothers

parts.text: Solomon marries Pharaoh’s daughter and brings her to Jerusalem. He loves the LORD, though sacrifice continues at high places because the temple is not yet built. At Gibeon, God appears in a dream and invites a request. Solomon asks for an understanding heart to judge the people. God grants extraordinary wisdom and also riches and honour, with long life conditioned upon obedience. Solomon returns to Jerusalem and offers sacrifices.

Two women claim the same living baby after one child dies in the night. Solomon orders the living child divided, revealing the true mother through her willingness to surrender him rather than see him killed. He gives her the child. Israel hears the judgment and recognizes God’s wisdom in its king.

chapters.title: Solomon’s ordered kingdom and renowned wisdom

parts.text: Solomon’s chief officers and twelve regional providers are named. Each provider supplies the royal household for one month of the year, distributing the burden across the kingdom. The account identifies their territories and family connections, showing the administration supporting Solomon’s rule over all Israel.

Judah and Israel prosper, eat, drink, and rejoice. Solomon rules over surrounding kingdoms that bring tribute, and the people dwell safely under their vines and fig trees. The chapter describes the court’s extensive daily provisions, horses, and chariots. God gives Solomon exceptional wisdom and breadth of understanding. He speaks proverbs and songs and discusses plants and animals, drawing visitors from many peoples and kings who hear of his wisdom.

chapters.title: Preparations to build the temple

parts.text: Hiram of Tyre sends servants to Solomon because of his friendship with David. Solomon explains that God has given him rest from enemies, allowing him to build the house promised to David’s son. He requests cedar timber and offers wages for Hiram’s skilled workers. Hiram rejoices, agrees to supply cedar and fir by sea, and receives food for his household in return. Peace and a treaty join the kings.

Solomon organizes a large workforce, sending rotating labourers to Lebanon and appointing bearers, stonecutters, and overseers. Great costly stones are quarried for the temple’s foundation. Solomon’s builders, Hiram’s builders, and the stonesquarers prepare both timber and stone, assembling the materials needed before construction proceeds.

chapters.title: The temple is built according to its design

parts.text: Solomon begins the LORD’s house in his fourth year, stated as the 480th year after Israel’s departure from Egypt. The account describes the building’s dimensions, porch, windows, and surrounding chambers. Stones are prepared before arrival so iron tools are not heard during construction. God tells Solomon that if he obeys his statutes and commandments, the promise to David will stand and God will dwell among Israel.

The interior is lined with cedar and overlaid with gold, with carvings of cherubims, palm trees, and flowers. The innermost room receives two large olive-wood cherubims whose wings span the sanctuary. Doors, floor coverings, and the inner court are described. The house is completed in Solomon’s eleventh year, after seven years of building.

chapters.title: The palace complex and temple furnishings

parts.text: Solomon builds his own house over thirteen years, including the house of the forest of Lebanon, halls for judgment, and a residence for Pharaoh’s daughter. The account describes costly stone and cedar construction. A skilled brass worker named Hiram is brought from Tyre to make temple fittings, beginning with two ornate pillars named Jachin and Boaz.

Hiram makes the great molten sea supported by twelve oxen, ten wheeled bases with lavers, and many utensils. Their decorations include lions, oxen, cherubims, palms, and flowers. Brass objects are cast in the Jordan plain in great abundance. Solomon also provides gold furnishings for the temple, including the altar, table, candlesticks, and vessels. David’s dedicated treasures are placed in the completed house.

chapters.title: The ark enters the temple and Solomon prays

parts.text: Solomon gathers Israel’s leaders to bring the ark into the temple’s inner sanctuary beneath the cherubims. The priests withdraw as a cloud fills the house with the LORD’s glory. Solomon blesses the congregation and recounts how God fulfilled his word to David by allowing his son to build the house for his name.

In prayer, Solomon acknowledges that even heaven cannot contain God. He asks him to hear prayers directed toward this house, judging disputes, forgiving repentant sinners, and answering during defeat, drought, famine, exile, and war. He includes the stranger who comes because of God’s name. Solomon urges Israel’s wholehearted obedience, offers abundant sacrifices, and celebrates with a great assembly. The people depart rejoicing in God’s goodness to David and Israel.

chapters.title: God’s warning and Solomon’s building works

parts.text: After Solomon completes the temple and palace, the LORD appears to him again. He accepts the dedicated house and promises enduring attention to it. If Solomon walks faithfully like David, God will establish his throne. But if he or his descendants turn to other gods, Israel will be cut off and the temple rejected. Its desolation will become a warning explained by Israel’s forsaking of the LORD.

The chapter records Solomon’s dealings with Hiram, including cities Hiram finds displeasing, and describes building projects such as Jerusalem’s walls, fortified towns, and storage cities. Remaining Canaanite peoples supply bondservice, while Israelites hold military and supervisory roles. Solomon continues sacrifices at the temple and develops a fleet with Hiram’s sailors, bringing gold from Ophir.

chapters.title: The queen of Sheba visits Solomon

parts.text: The queen of Sheba comes with a rich caravan to test Solomon with difficult questions after hearing his fame concerning the LORD’s name. He answers everything, and the wisdom, ordered court, provisions, and worship she sees exceed her expectations. She blesses the LORD for placing him over Israel to do judgment and justice. They exchange generous gifts, and she returns to her country.

The account describes Solomon’s immense gold revenues, gold shields, ivory-and-gold throne, precious vessels, and far-reaching trade. His wealth and wisdom attract rulers and yearly gifts from many lands. Horses and chariots multiply, and silver becomes commonplace in Jerusalem. Trade with Egypt supplies horses and chariots that are also distributed to neighbouring kings.

chapters.title: Solomon turns to other gods and adversaries arise

parts.text: Solomon loves many foreign wives from nations God warned Israel not to marry. In his old age they turn his heart toward their gods, and he builds high places for their worship. Because he forsakes the LORD’s command despite two divine appearances, God announces that most of the kingdom will be torn from his son, preserving a portion for David’s sake and Jerusalem’s sake.

God raises adversaries including Hadad of Edom and Rezon of Damascus. Jeroboam, a capable officer, receives a message from Ahijah, who tears a garment into twelve pieces and gives him ten, promising a kingdom and conditional blessing for obedience. Solomon seeks Jeroboam’s death, and he flees to Egypt. Solomon dies after forty years, and Rehoboam succeeds him.

chapters.title: The kingdom divides and Jeroboam makes golden calves

parts.text: At Shechem, the people ask Rehoboam to lighten Solomon’s heavy burdens. He rejects the elders’ counsel for the harsher advice of younger companions and threatens increased oppression. The northern tribes rebel, rejecting David’s house, and stone the officer sent over forced labour. Rehoboam flees to Jerusalem, while Israel makes Jeroboam king. The division fulfils the LORD’s word through Ahijah.

Rehoboam gathers an army, but God forbids civil war, and the men return home. Jeroboam fears that worship at Jerusalem will restore allegiance to David’s house. He makes golden calves at Beth-el and Dan, establishes unauthorized priests and high places, and invents a feast in the eighth month. These arrangements become sin to Israel as he approaches the altar at Beth-el.

chapters.title: The man of God and the danger of disobedience

parts.text: A man of God from Judah confronts Jeroboam’s altar at Beth-el, announcing that a future son of David named Josiah will defile it. The altar splits as a sign. Jeroboam’s outstretched hand withers and is restored after the prophet prays. The man refuses the king’s hospitality because God commanded him not to eat, drink, or return by the same route.

An old prophet deceives him with a claimed angelic instruction to return and eat. While they eat, the LORD announces judgment for disobeying the original command. A lion kills the man on his way but does not eat his body or attack the ass. The old prophet buries him and affirms his prophecy against the altar. Jeroboam nevertheless continues appointing unauthorized priests, bringing destruction upon his house.

chapters.title: Judgment on Jeroboam and Rehoboam’s unfaithfulness

parts.text: Jeroboam sends his disguised wife to the blind prophet Ahijah concerning their sick son. God reveals her identity beforehand. Ahijah announces destruction upon Jeroboam’s house because he made idols and led Israel into sin. The child will die as his mother returns, though he alone receives honourable mourning because something good toward the LORD was found in him. Ahijah also foretells Israel’s scattering. Jeroboam later dies, and Nadab succeeds him.

Rehoboam’s Judah also practices idolatry and abominations. Shishak of Egypt attacks Jerusalem and takes the temple and palace treasures, including Solomon’s gold shields, which are replaced with brass. The chapter records continuing hostility between Rehoboam and Jeroboam. Rehoboam dies and is succeeded by Abijam.

chapters.title: Judah’s contrasting kings and Israel’s dynastic violence

parts.text: Abijam follows his father’s sins, but God preserves David’s lamp in Jerusalem. Asa succeeds him and does right, removing idols and immoral worship practices and deposing Maachah from her royal position because of her idol. Yet the high places remain. When Baasha fortifies Ramah against Judah, Asa buys Syrian assistance with sacred and royal treasures, forcing Baasha to withdraw. Asa later suffers disease in his feet and is succeeded by Jehoshaphat.

In Israel, Nadab continues Jeroboam’s sins. Baasha assassinates him during a siege and destroys Jeroboam’s entire house, fulfilling Ahijah’s prophecy. Baasha then rules Israel but repeats the same idolatrous pattern. War continues between his kingdom and Asa’s throughout their reigns.

chapters.title: Repeated coups and Ahab’s deeper apostasy

parts.text: Through Jehu the prophet, God announces judgment on Baasha’s house because he follows Jeroboam’s sins. Elah succeeds Baasha but is killed by Zimri, who destroys the royal household. The army then proclaims Omri king. After only seven days, Zimri is besieged and burns the palace over himself. His end follows his sins and rebellion.

A division between Omri and Tibni ends with Omri prevailing. He builds Samaria and does worse than earlier kings. His son Ahab goes further, marrying Jezebel, serving Baal, building his temple in Samaria, and provoking the LORD beyond his predecessors. During Ahab’s reign, Hiel rebuilds Jericho at the cost of his firstborn and youngest sons, fulfilling the word spoken through Joshua.

chapters.title: Elijah is sustained and restores a widow’s son

parts.text: Elijah tells Ahab there will be neither dew nor rain except by his word. God sends him to the brook Cherith, where ravens bring food. When the brook dries, he goes to Zarephath and asks a widow for food. She has only enough meal and oil for a final meal, but follows Elijah’s promise. Her supplies do not fail throughout the drought, according to the LORD’s word.

The widow’s son becomes sick and dies. She fears Elijah has brought her sin to remembrance. He carries the child upstairs, cries to God, and stretches himself upon him three times. God hears, the child’s soul returns, and Elijah restores him alive to his mother. She affirms that Elijah is a man of God and the LORD’s word in his mouth is truth.

chapters.title: The LORD answers by fire and sends rain

parts.text: God sends Elijah back to Ahab in the third year, promising rain. Elijah meets Obadiah, who has secretly preserved the LORD’s prophets from Jezebel. After assurances, Obadiah brings Ahab. Elijah rejects the accusation that he troubles Israel, identifying the king’s abandonment of God’s commands, and summons Israel and Baal’s prophets to Carmel.

Elijah challenges the people to choose between the LORD and Baal. Baal’s prophets receive no answer despite prolonged cries and self-cutting. Elijah repairs the LORD’s altar, drenches the sacrifice and trench with water, and prays. God’s fire consumes everything, and the people acknowledge him. Elijah executes Baal’s prophets, then prays for rain. A small cloud appears, a heavy storm follows, and Elijah runs before Ahab to Jezreel.

chapters.title: Elijah at Horeb and Elisha’s call

parts.text: Jezebel threatens Elijah after hearing of Carmel. He flees, leaves his servant, and asks to die in the wilderness, feeling no better than his fathers. An angel supplies food and water twice, strengthening him for forty days and nights to Horeb.

In a cave at Horeb, God questions Elijah’s claim that he alone remains faithful. A great wind, earthquake, and fire pass, but the LORD is not in them; afterward comes a still small voice. God sends him back with instructions concerning Hazael, Jehu, and Elisha and declares that seven thousand in Israel have not bowed to Baal. Elijah finds Elisha plowing and casts his mantle upon him. Elisha leaves his former work, provides a farewell meal, and becomes Elijah’s servant.

chapters.title: Ahab defeats Syria but spares Ben-hadad

parts.text: Ben-hadad and allied kings besiege Samaria, demanding Ahab’s wealth and family. Ahab initially submits but rejects an expanded demand to search and plunder the city. A prophet promises victory so Ahab will know the LORD. Following the given instructions, Israel attacks while the Syrians are drinking and routs them. The prophet warns Ahab to prepare for another attack.

The Syrians attribute their loss to Israel’s God being a god of hills and fight again on the plain. God grants another victory to expose that claim. Ben-hadad’s servants seek mercy, and Ahab makes a treaty and releases him. A prophet confronts Ahab through a staged case and declares that his own life and people will answer for releasing the man appointed to destruction. Ahab returns resentful.

chapters.title: Naboth’s vineyard and judgment on Ahab

parts.text: Ahab wants Naboth’s vineyard beside his palace, offering money or another vineyard. Naboth refuses to surrender his ancestral inheritance, and Ahab sulks. Jezebel uses the king’s authority to arrange a fast, false witnesses, and a charge that Naboth cursed God and the king. Naboth is stoned, and Jezebel tells Ahab to take possession of the vineyard.

The LORD sends Elijah to confront Ahab for murder and seizure. He announces disgrace, destruction of Ahab’s house, and Jezebel’s death by dogs, identifying Ahab’s exceptional wickedness under her influence. Ahab responds by tearing his clothes, fasting, and humbling himself. God acknowledges this humiliation and postpones the announced disaster upon the household until his son’s days.

chapters.title: Micaiah’s warning and Ahab’s death

parts.text: Ahab invites Jehoshaphat of Judah to attack Ramoth-gilead. Numerous prophets promise success, but Jehoshaphat asks for a prophet of the LORD. Micaiah foretells Israel scattered without a shepherd and describes a heavenly scene in which a lying spirit deceives Ahab’s prophets. Despite mistreatment and imprisonment, he maintains that Ahab’s safe return would disprove his message.

Ahab disguises himself in battle, but an arrow strikes him between armour joints, and he dies. Dogs lick his blood as foretold. The account then reviews Jehoshaphat’s generally faithful rule, remaining high places, peace with Israel, and failed shipping venture. After his death, Jehoram succeeds him in Judah. Ahab’s son Ahaziah rules Israel and follows his parents’ and Jeroboam’s evil worship.
